issues.where: clouds across the western half of the globe and near the left limb (image-06 D, F; image-07 M, N, R)
issues.what: clouds break up into small square blocks and smeared rectangles, like low-res tiles or compression blocks; you can see pixels and tile edges at native size
issues.fix: use a higher-resolution cloud layer with mipmapping or filtering, and remove the blocky upscale or temporal artifact before you output the frame

issues.where: bottom third of the frame: South America, the Pacific clouds and the night side (image-08 S, T, U; image-06 E, G)
issues.what: heavy directional smearing and streaks: the land, clouds and city lights are dragged into lines, so the near terrain is soft and the detail is gone
issues.fix: cut or remove the motion blur or warp at the bottom of the frame, or render it with correct per-pixel motion vectors, so the surface stays sharp

issues.where: Caribbean, Gulf of Mexico and Central America (image-06 A, I; image-07 O)
issues.what: hundreds of tiny bright cloud specks sit on the water like scattered white pixels or noise. They look like confetti, not cumulus
issues.fix: filter the cloud mask and drop the isolated speckles, or blend the small clouds softly into the layer

issues.where: Rockies and Andes (image-07 J; image-06 B, G)
issues.what: the terrain looks like plastic relief extruded straight up from a heightmap, with stepped ridges and too much contrast, so it looks like a clay model at native size
issues.fix: lower the displacement exaggeration, soften the normal map, and add subtle atmospheric scattering over the land

issues.where: upper right limb, the aurora (image-02 C; image-03 L, M)
issues.what: the aurora is a flat green band painted along the limb, with a uniform comb of streaks and a red haze behind it. It reads as a separate layer stuck on, with no depth or curvature into the atmosphere
issues.fix: make the aurora a volumetric curtain that follows the shape of the oval, with height falloff and varying brightness and spacing, and blend it into the limb glow

issues.where: right edge of the night side (image-02 E, I; image-03 R)
issues.what: the night limb has a hard edge with no atmosphere, and a lighter band or doubled edge near the silhouette makes it look like two layered discs
issues.fix: carry a thin atmosphere rim onto the night side and fix the offset between the shadowed globe and the surface layer

issues.what: city lights shine on ground that is still in daylight. The night lights layer is masked wrong for the terminator
issues.fix: drive the night lights mask from the sun angle so the lights only appear past the terminator, with a soft blend

issues.where: Atlantic and Pacific cloud swirls (image-02 A, F; image-03 L)
issues.what: the swirls repeat the same spiral shape over and over and look airbrushed. The clouds feel stamped on, not like real weather
issues.fix: vary the shapes of the cloud systems and use real or more varied cloud data

issues.what: the star field is a dense orange speckle patch that looks like noise, not stars
issues.fix: use a star field with proper point stars and a gentle, smooth falloff in density

issues.what: the moon is small and slightly soft, with flat shading and only a little surface detail
issues.fix: use a sharper texture on the moon and give it a crisper terminator

issues.where: lower half and outer flanks of the globe (image-14.png crops D, E, F, H; image-15.png crops O, P, Q; image-16.png crops S, T, U, V)
issues.what: heavy stepped radial smear and blocky directional blur stretch the Pacific clouds, Amazon and Andes terrain, and Brazilian coastal city lights into pixelated streaks while adjacent background stars remain pin-sharp
issues.fix: remove the undersampled radial or motion blur on the globe pass, or increase motion-blur sampling and apply consistent camera blur across all composited layers

issues.where: northern and central Atlantic globe surface and clouds (image-14.png crop C; image-15.png crops L, Q)
issues.what: clouds and ocean surface are soft, muddy, and low-resolution compared with the crisp North American continent
issues.fix: use higher-resolution cloud and ocean maps on the Atlantic side and match sharpness across the full visible hemisphere

issues.where: upper right aurora along the limb (image-14.png crop C; image-15.png crop L)
issues.what: aurora curtains look airbrushed and show horizontal stepped banding at the base of the brightest green ray near the limb
issues.fix: render the aurora with finer volumetric ray structure, higher bit-depth alpha falloff, and smooth integration into the atmospheric limb

issues.where: upper left Milky Way sky region (image-14.png crops B, G)
issues.what: dust lanes have coarse stippled noise and posterized blotches, and dense stars merge into blocky blobs with an abrupt transition to clean black sky
issues.fix: replace or denoise the Milky Way background plate at higher native resolution, keep star point-spread profiles crisp, and feather the galactic dust falloff

issues.where: night-side right limb and western mountain ranges (image-15.png crops J, P, R; image-16.png crop V)
issues.what: mountain relief on western North America and the northern Andes looks slightly embossed and plastic, and the dark night limb shows a faint thin greenish-cyan rim line against the starfield
issues.fix: reduce normal or displacement exaggeration on continental relief and soften the night-side atmospheric rim falloff

issues.where: upper-center dark sky above the limb and coastal land (image-11.png crops K, L, Q, R; image-10.png crop I)
issues.what: the solar-glow falloff in the upper sky shows faint concentric gradient banding and subtle color blotching, and inland island terrain is slightly painterly next to crisp clouds
issues.fix: dither the high-dynamic-range sky flare gradient in 16-bit before output and sharpen fine land-cover detail on the islands
